The Paper Inside the Coat

外套夹层里的那张纸 · 586 词 · 7 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1Police arrested Leon, a juvenile, after a shop burglary. A witness had seen a green sleeve while the burglar assaulted the owner. A sergeant found a similar coat at Leon's home. During interrogation he treated the match as proof. Leon's solicitor warned that an indictment could entail years of imprisonment. Leon made a guilty plea, hoping for leniency. Years later, while on parole, he met a court aide who helped former inmates find work. She wondered why his file linked him to a coat he had bought secondhand.

2The aide requested judicial review to find out whether a mistake in the file had led the state to imprison the wrong person. A statute allowed an old conviction to be overturned if important evidence emerged. The prosecutor called the request a waste of time. She did not seek to indict the sergeant or prove malice in the judiciary. She wanted to interrogate the evidence itself. The officer's report had dismissed Leon's account as evasive. It recorded that he claimed to have a receipt but could not find it. The aide asked whether the coat still existed.

3The storehouse kept it in a carton. One seam had split, revealing a thin piece of paper beneath the lining. The aide asked a custodian to record the discovery before she touched it. It was a receipt from a charity shop, dated before the burglary. The ink was feeble but legible. A repair described on the back tied it to that coat. The charity worker had replaced a brass clasp and sewn a crooked stitch beside the pocket.

4The prosecution said a receipt did not settle who wore the sleeve. The aide examined a stock sheet that a shop assistant had kept. Every stolen coat had a silver zipper. Leon's brass clasp matched none of them. The sheet had never been given to his solicitor. Under a statutory rule, the prosecution had to disclose material that could help the defense. A lawyer said the omission had made Leon plead guilty without knowing a fact that might have led a jury to acquit him.

5At the hearing the original witness testified again. She said she had never seen the burglar's face. A prosecutor asked whether harassment had prompted the change. Had anyone tried to harass her? She described the same green sleeve that had been in her first statement. The aide had not asked her to alter it. The judges could now see how a glimpse of fabric had become a claim about a person. The unanimous decision overturned the conviction. The prosecution would not seek to convict Leon again.

6A separate panel considered a sanction to deter anyone from withholding evidence. Leon asked if he could sue for malpractice. His lawyer said the verdict opened that possibility. An infringement of his rights might warrant compensation. The aide helped remove a restriction that had kept him from applying for work. The change did not return the years he had spent under detention or on parole. It let him decide what to do next without someone else setting the deadline.

7At the charity shop Leon found the volunteer who had written the receipt. She remembered the crooked stitch and joked that it had given the paper a place to hide. The aide hoped the case would set a precedent. Leon wanted to thank the person who had written down the clasp when she could have written only "coat." A small act of care had survived inside the lining until someone thought to look.

六级大纲词汇 · 17中文译文

外套夹层里的那张纸

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一家店发生入室盗窃，警方逮捕了少年利昂。窃贼袭击店主时，证人看见了一截绿色袖子。一名警长在利昂家找到一件相似的外套，在讯问时把相似当成了证据。律师告诉利昂，一旦被起诉，他可能要坐几年牢。利昂选择认罪，希望从轻处理。几年后，他获准假释，遇到一位帮出狱人员找工作的司法助理。她不明白，案卷为什么把他和一件他从二手店买来的外套联系在一起。

2助理申请司法复核，想查清是否因为案卷里的错误，有人被错关进了监狱。一条法律规定，出现重要证据时，可以推翻过去的定罪。检察官说，复核是在浪费时间。助理只想重新查验证据。她无意起诉那名警长，也没打算证明司法机关存有恶意。警方报告称利昂在回避问题，还记下他说自己本有收据，只是找不到了。助理问，那件外套还在不在。

3外套装在库房的一只纸盒里。一道缝裂开，露出夹层里一张薄纸。助理请保管员先记录发现过程，再伸手去取。那是一张慈善商店的收据，日期早于盗窃案。墨迹虽淡，还能辨认。收据背面写着一次修补的细节，能证明它对应的是这件衣服。店员换过一枚黄铜搭扣，还在口袋旁缝了一针，针脚有点歪。

4控方说，收据不能证明当时穿那件衣服的是谁。助理看了店员留下的库存表。每件失窃外套用的都是银色拉链，利昂那件的黄铜搭扣和它们都不一样。利昂的律师当年从没收到那张表。按规定，控方必须披露有助于辩护的材料。一名律师说，漏掉这份证据，让利昂在不知道一个重要事实的情况下认罪。那个事实本来有可能让陪审团宣告他无罪。

5听证会上，原来的证人再次作证。她说自己从没看见窃贼的脸。检察官问，有没有人骚扰她，想让她改口。她描述的仍是最初证词里的那截绿袖子，助理从未要求她改变说法。法官们终于看清，瞥见一截布料，怎么逐渐变成了对一个人的指认。法院一致推翻了原判，控方也不再请求给利昂定罪。

6另一个小组研究是否该作出处罚，以防有人再隐瞒证据。利昂问，自己能否就失职提起诉讼。律师说，新的裁定让这成为可能。权利受到侵害，可能有理由寻求赔偿。助理先帮他取消了妨碍他求职的一项限制。被羁押和假释的年月回不来了，但接下来该做什么，可以由他自己决定。

7利昂回到慈善商店，找到了开收据的志愿者。她记得那针缝歪了，还开玩笑说，多亏它给那张纸留下了藏身处。助理希望这个案子能成为先例。利昂想感谢的，是那个本来只写“外套”就够了，却愿意记下一枚搭扣的人。那点细心一直留在夹层里，直到有人想起来找它。
